approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a population of at most sixty-four accepted molecules, kept in descending score order. It chooses a high-ranking score band and then a molecule uniformly within that band, produces a fresh surplus of crossover and mutation offspring, and uses correlated draws from a fingerprint Gaussian process to choose which offspring to evaluate. Every accepted score trains the posterior, even if its molecule leaves the breeding population. This loop reliably learns and selects, but most evaluated offspring do not improve on their generating parents, and successful molecular cores accumulate many close relatives.
approach.novelty: Give each represented molecular core equal breeding probability within the already selected score band. A core with many surviving analogues will share its probability among those analogues, while a less represented accepted core gains an opportunity to breed. The existing preference for high-scoring bands remains intact. The lineage's earlier child changed how generated offspring are selected for evaluation; this child changes only which accepted parents produce those offspring. Neither recorded sibling nor a supplied mechanism cluster has tested this conditional correction for core multiplicity.

hypothesis: Within each inherited score quantile, sample accepted breeding parents with probability inversely proportional to the number of eligible survivors sharing their Murcko core, so every represented core has equal conditional mass.

finding_summary.headline: Core-balanced breeding broadened core use and raised parent-beating yield, but lowered final scores.
finding_summary.insights:
Equalizing core probability can reduce repeated use of abundant families without improving the best molecules found. The clearest coverage expansions were in decoration hopping and DRD2, yet their parent-beating counts and final-score means fell. Zaleplon breeding became more concentrated despite correct balancing within each selected band, showing that changing the conditional draw does not guarantee broader realized coverage once the evolving survivor population is considered.

The modest parent-beating gain also uses a weaker reference: mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.419645 to 0.395720, while mean evaluated-offspring score fell from 0.319152 to 0.301731. This relative yield gain therefore does not establish stronger offspring production. The number of admitted offspring later reused for breeding stayed almost unchanged, at 2,163 versus 2,167, and incumbent gains did not increase. The evidence narrows the problem to allocating toward productive surviving families rather than simply reducing their multiplicity imbalance; discarded or ineligible cores still receive no opportunity. The molecular assessment also shows that broader structural coverage continues to include repeated heterocycle growth, tiny fragments, reactive nitrogen-halogen/peroxide groups and strained fused rings. Murcko-core coverage alone does not resolve those quality limitations. Passive comparisons supply probabilities and parent identities, with no scores for alternate offspring or an alternate search trajectory.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation change executed correctly in all three replicas. Of 111,246 parent draws, 86,634 had unequal core multiplicities; every logged probability vector and inverse-CDF choice matched the intended rule. On the same eligible states and logged uniform variates, 36,398 selected parent ranks and 29,554 selected cores differed from the passive uniform comparator. Mean represented cores used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 14.60, and mean concentration of breeding uses fell from 0.299 to 0.189, measured as the sum of squared core-use shares. Coverage rose in 10 of 15 task/seed sessions; the effect was not universal. All accepted-state, survivor and pending-provenance checks passed, and both panels completed all 4,500 oracle evaluations.

Strict best-parent beats increased from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 600/4,350 (13.79%), and mean child-minus-best-parent score improved from -0.100493 to -0.093989. Incumbent improvements were nearly unchanged, at 216 versus 218. Mean final-best score across tasks and seeds fell from 0.544374 to 0.524118, a paired change of -0.020256. Seed changes were -0.052822, -0.023812 and +0.015865; all five task means declined. Thus the intended allocation mechanism is confirmed, while the intended score increase was not observed.

molecular.headline: Repeated heterocycle growth and tiny fragments coexist with reactive, highly fused leading molecules
molecular.overall_character: The current panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete three-seed Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9425 to 0.9931 and ring-closure presence from 0.977 to 0.9931; charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These are string-presence measurements, not aromatic atom fractions, ionization measurements or evidence of feasible stereochemistry. The output is ring-rich and often extensively aromatic: fused nitrogen carbonyl systems, aromatic amine/aminal frameworks and halogenated unsaturated heterocycles dominate the leaders. Chemical scale varies from tiny fragments to large assemblies of repeated heterocycles. This is particularly pronounced in deco_hop, whose mean SMILES length is 115.4 and maximum is 235; its seed-2 final molecules visibly repeat nitrogen-dione units. The Parent also produced reactive and extensively connected structures. Current leaders retain N-halogen bonds, peroxide or hypohalite motifs, tight ring fusion and unspecified configurations. Overall synthetic plausibility is questionable, with strongly implausible individual small-ring or growth outliers, and drug-like quality remains weak. Across-seed diversity is moderate; many late streams mainly elaborate a common core.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecules are moderately sized fused unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles bearing fluoroaryl carboxamides, alkyl/alkoxy substituents and hydroxymethyl or aminomethyl groups. Amide N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and fused-ring N-F are frequent in the leaders. Seed 0 reaches pyrazole thioamides with phenolic, cyclopentadienyl and cyclobutenyl groups; seed 1 reaches an aryl ketone with N-O/N-N functionality. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9782 and halogen presence is 0.7149. Relative to the Parent aromatic ketone, amide and thioheterocyclic families, the compact aromatic/carbonyl theme persists, with reactive nitrogen substitution and unusual ring geometry.
liabilities: N-Br, N-Cl and N-F bonds add reactivity to amide and ring nitrogens; N-O/N-N variants add compatibility concerns.
Unusual unsaturated small rings, scaffold doubling and very small fragment products reduce the chemical coherence of the output.
missing_features: Stable nonhalogenated nitrogen alternatives preserving the successful aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are poorly represented among the leading amide series.

Accessible fused-ring alternatives and explicit configurations or alkene geometry are absent for many unusual partially saturated and bridged products; a unique target pharmacophore cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best N-bromoamide/N-fluoro heterocycle scores 0.4294168350924388 versus 0.4163503402962837 for the paired Parent seed 2; other paired seeds change in different directions. N-Cl, N-F and N-Br amide variants share 0.41885833432199493, so their reactivity is not distinguished. A halogen-free pyrazole thioamide reaches 0.4220190409118175, showing N-halogen chemistry is not universally required in this region. Tiny peroxide or halogen compounds score 0.0, and an isolated fluoro-carbamoyl fragment scores 9.818532642967522e-13. The complete ring/carbonyl arrangement matters more than a reactive group in a tiny fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 family is a relatively compact fused aza-heteroaromatic carbonyl system joined to fluorinated nitrogen heteroaryl rings. It bears a cyclic peroxide bridge and alkyl, vinyl or ethynyl substituents. In contrast, seed 0 and especially seed 2 produce large structures with repeated nitrogen-dione/heteroaryl modules, ester/ketone connections and many aromatic rings; some final products also contain N-Br. Aromatic and ring-closure presence are 0.9931 and halogen presence is 0.8575. The Parent also favored reactive fused heterocycles and expanded dione assemblies. Here the highest score occurs in the more compact seed-1 family rather than the large repeated assemblies.
liabilities: Cyclic peroxide, N-halogen and reactive linker motifs complicate stability and synthesis.
Very large repeated heterocycle assemblies create substantial size, aromaticity, flexibility and synthetic-complexity liabilities.
missing_features: Compact stable alternatives preserving the favorable heteroaryl/carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented relative to peroxide-bearing or repeatedly expanded structures.
The late growth families lack a demonstrated need for repeated dione units, extra aromatic attachments and ester-linked duplication.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best peroxide-containing fused heterocycle scores 0.616390401531925, compared with the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.6324703199409752. Vinyl, ethynyl and methyl derivatives tie at 0.6152337858220212. Removing a peroxide oxygen from the vinyl compound gives 0.6151026837099413, demonstrating a near-equivalent nonperoxide alternative. Much larger seed-2 assemblies remain around 0.59, with a maximum of 0.5995098039215686, while tiny fluorine or hydrocarbon fragments score 0.5. The recurring nitrogen/carbonyl/heteroaryl arrangement appears favorable, without evidence that repeated growth or peroxide functionality is necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders combine halogenated aromatic rings with nitrogen-rich saturated rings, secondary methylamino groups and compact fused aminal frameworks. The best seed-2 family contains a small diazetidine-like unit and aryl N-Cl; seed 1 also gives sulfinamide-linked bicyclic diamines or densely fused carbon/nitrogen rings. Fluoromethoxy groups have carbon-bound fluorine, while other members carry the distinct reactive aryl O-F motif. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9839 and halogen presence is 0.992. The Parent similarly produced aromatic amines with constrained rings. Current synthesis remains questionable because of tight junctions and reactive substituents.
liabilities: Tight small-ring aminal fusion and unspecified configurations create substantial geometric and synthetic uncertainty.
Aryl N-Cl and O-F bonds, occasional unusual sulfur bonding and bulky aromatic substitution remain chemical or physicochemical liabilities.
missing_features: Accessible less constrained cyclic-amine and aminal geometries preserving the favorable aromatic spacing are underrepresented among the leaders.
Defined stereochemistry at fused junctions and sulfinamide sulfur, together with relevant protonation alternatives, is absent from the displayed comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best N-chloro fused aromatic aminal scores 0.9557660498629175 versus 0.9914038363125457 for the paired Parent seed 2. A sulfinamide/bicyclic-diamine member reaches 0.9490309869379135 without N-Cl or O-F, while a less connected aromatic aminal without N-Cl scores 0.9252905395110519. Early acidic amide derivatives score as low as 0.000719339566735797, and a small sulfur/N-Cl fragment scores 0.0017478706282521514. These observations favor the complete aromatic/amine arrangement rather than reactive halogen bonding alone. All current paired maxima are below their Parent counterparts.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are densely fused aromatic nitrogen polycycles with ethoxy, amino or alkyl substituents and attached or bridged lactam/dione regions. Some have N-O-containing rings or additional saturated bridges. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9816 and ring-closure presence is 0.9851; numerous fused aromatic rings are visible in the leaders. Sulfur and halogens are not major features of the best series. Relative to the Parent cyclic carbonyl, aryl-aza and amine frameworks, current output often contains more condensed fused aromatic connectivity, increasing planarity and synthetic complexity without a clear score advantage.
liabilities: Large fused aromatic surfaces create solubility and nonspecific-interaction concerns, while extensive ring connectivity complicates synthesis.
Bridge stereochemistry, unusual N-O/N-N connectivity in some variants and fragment-sized proposals remain unresolved quality issues.
missing_features: Simpler accessible frameworks preserving the favorable aromatic and carbonyl/nitrogen attachment pattern are underrepresented relative to condensed polycyclic growth.
Configurations are unspecified for saturated bridges and junctions, and the evidence does not show that additional fusion is needed over more flexible alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best amino/ethoxy fused polycyclic dione scores 0.21165206225960834 versus the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.22405709718343647; the other paired current maxima are also lower. Removing a carbonyl in a close late relative retains 0.2106565294702053. Another fused aryl/aza-lactam family reaches 0.20845479592460323. Tiny hydrocarbon or peroxide fragments score 0.0, while several more elaborate final variants remain below the leaders. The evidence favors an intact aromatic/polar-ring arrangement but does not identify a required single carbonyl or unique target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: Higher-scoring seed-2 compounds are moderately sized nitrogen-rich cyclic diones with imine-containing N-substituents, carbon-bound fluorine, N-F and a chlorofluorinated fused small-ring hydrocarbon partner. The best nitrogen dione has an expanded aromatic ring rather than a conventional small heterocycle. Seed 1 includes an activated ester attached to a cyclobutadiene-like ring and a fluorinated fused dione; other members contain lactones. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9425 and halogen presence is 0.8517. Large doubled or repeated dione/aryl assemblies occupy the low tail. The Parent also had favorable compact fluorinated carbonyl/nitrogen arrangements, but current N-F and strained-ring chemistry still limit plausibility.
liabilities: N-F, O-F, imine and activated unsaturated ester motifs introduce reactivity; the cyclobutadiene-like ring raises strong stability concerns.
Expanded nitrogen-rich aromatic rings, fused small-ring geometry and repeated dione growth lack established synthetic accessibility and stereochemical definition.
missing_features: Stable accessible alternatives retaining the favorable nitrogen/carbonyl/fluorinated arrangement without N-F or strained unsaturated small rings are not demonstrated among the leaders.
Configurations at fused hydrocarbon junctions and hydroxyl/fluoro-bearing sites are absent, while late doubled structures lose the compact favorable arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 maximum is 0.5197936759696083 versus 0.4071395189354175 for its Parent; the current maxima for the other seeds are lower. Adding a nitrogen within a close final dione ring lowers the score to 0.0839454186797069, showing sensitivity to local ring composition rather than nitrogen count. The cyclobutadiene-like ester scores 0.4852949787500649. Large coupled aromatic/dione products score as low as 1.6758614448245604e-53. Bounded size and particular carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorinated-ring placement appear favorable, but the observations do not establish reactive N-F or strained rings as chemically desirable solutions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest extremes include elemental or small hydrocarbon/peroxide molecules and repeated nitrogen-dione/heteroaryl assemblies. One proposal set has mean SMILES length 115.4 and maximum 235, while its highest score comes from a much smaller fused heterocycle.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a useful molecular scale between tiny fragments and repeated large assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make fragment retention, compact recombination and removal of repeated modules available while preserving useful attachment geometry. Repeated aromatic or carbonyl units should not dominate alternatives to an intact favorable scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring molecules contain N-Br/N-Cl/N-F, O-F and cyclic peroxide motifs. N-halogen variants tie at 0.41885833432199493; a peroxide-containing vinyl heterocycle at 0.6152337858220212 has a nonperoxide relative at 0.6151026837099413.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive halogen and peroxide bonds remain frequent substitutes for stable heteroatom chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable matched nitrogen and oxygen bonding alternatives around the same cores, and represent functional-group compatibility independently of scalar feedback. Some reactive bonds are demonstrably unnecessary to retain the observed favorable arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leaders include tightly fused aminal rings, extensive aromatic condensation, expanded nitrogen diones and a cyclobutadiene-like motif. Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 throughout despite saturated ring junctions and sulfur centres requiring configurational consideration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-rich generation is not matched by reliable ring geometry or stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish accessible small and fused rings from strongly strained unsaturation or incompatible junctions, and support configuration assignment and stereoisomer variation. Current trajectories do not establish stereochemical score sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A less connected aromatic aminal retains 0.9252905395110519, a fused relative with a removed carbonyl retains 0.2106565294702053, and methyl/vinyl/ethynyl heterocycle variants share 0.6152337858220212. Larger repeated or more fused products do not consistently improve scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring regions contain too few simple alternatives relative to the fusion and decoration explored.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand simpler linker, ring and substituent variants around recurring aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements. Score-tolerant regions could then contain more accessible and chemically interpretable molecules.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Core-balanced breeding broadened core use and raised parent-beating yield, but lowered final scores.
finding_summary.insights:
Equalizing core probability can reduce repeated use of abundant families without improving the best molecules found. The clearest coverage expansions were in decoration hopping and DRD2, yet their parent-beating counts and final-score means fell. Zaleplon breeding became more concentrated despite correct balancing within each selected band, showing that changing the conditional draw does not guarantee broader realized coverage once the evolving survivor population is considered.

The modest parent-beating gain also uses a weaker reference: mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.419645 to 0.395720, while mean evaluated-offspring score fell from 0.319152 to 0.301731. This relative yield gain therefore does not establish stronger offspring production. The number of admitted offspring later reused for breeding stayed almost unchanged, at 2,163 versus 2,167, and incumbent gains did not increase. The evidence narrows the problem to allocating toward productive surviving families rather than simply reducing their multiplicity imbalance; discarded or ineligible cores still receive no opportunity. The molecular assessment also shows that broader structural coverage continues to include repeated heterocycle growth, tiny fragments, reactive nitrogen-halogen/peroxide groups and strained fused rings. Murcko-core coverage alone does not resolve those quality limitations. Passive comparisons supply probabilities and parent identities, with no scores for alternate offspring or an alternate search trajectory.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation change executed correctly in all three replicas. Of 111,246 parent draws, 86,634 had unequal core multiplicities; every logged probability vector and inverse-CDF choice matched the intended rule. On the same eligible states and logged uniform variates, 36,398 selected parent ranks and 29,554 selected cores differed from the passive uniform comparator. Mean represented cores used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 14.60, and mean concentration of breeding uses fell from 0.299 to 0.189, measured as the sum of squared core-use shares. Coverage rose in 10 of 15 task/seed sessions; the effect was not universal. All accepted-state, survivor and pending-provenance checks passed, and both panels completed all 4,500 oracle evaluations.

Strict best-parent beats increased from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 600/4,350 (13.79%), and mean child-minus-best-parent score improved from -0.100493 to -0.093989. Incumbent improvements were nearly unchanged, at 216 versus 218. Mean final-best score across tasks and seeds fell from 0.544374 to 0.524118, a paired change of -0.020256. Seed changes were -0.052822, -0.023812 and +0.015865; all five task means declined. Thus the intended allocation mechanism is confirmed, while the intended score increase was not observed.

finding_summary.headline: Core-balanced breeding broadened core use and raised parent-beating yield, but lowered final scores.
finding_summary.insights:
Equalizing core probability can reduce repeated use of abundant families without improving the best molecules found. The clearest coverage expansions were in decoration hopping and DRD2, yet their parent-beating counts and final-score means fell. Zaleplon breeding became more concentrated despite correct balancing within each selected band, showing that changing the conditional draw does not guarantee broader realized coverage once the evolving survivor population is considered.

The modest parent-beating gain also uses a weaker reference: mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.419645 to 0.395720, while mean evaluated-offspring score fell from 0.319152 to 0.301731. This relative yield gain therefore does not establish stronger offspring production. The number of admitted offspring later reused for breeding stayed almost unchanged, at 2,163 versus 2,167, and incumbent gains did not increase. The evidence narrows the problem to allocating toward productive surviving families rather than simply reducing their multiplicity imbalance; discarded or ineligible cores still receive no opportunity. The molecular assessment also shows that broader structural coverage continues to include repeated heterocycle growth, tiny fragments, reactive nitrogen-halogen/peroxide groups and strained fused rings. Murcko-core coverage alone does not resolve those quality limitations. Passive comparisons supply probabilities and parent identities, with no scores for alternate offspring or an alternate search trajectory.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation change executed correctly in all three replicas. Of 111,246 parent draws, 86,634 had unequal core multiplicities; every logged probability vector and inverse-CDF choice matched the intended rule. On the same eligible states and logged uniform variates, 36,398 selected parent ranks and 29,554 selected cores differed from the passive uniform comparator. Mean represented cores used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 14.60, and mean concentration of breeding uses fell from 0.299 to 0.189, measured as the sum of squared core-use shares. Coverage rose in 10 of 15 task/seed sessions; the effect was not universal. All accepted-state, survivor and pending-provenance checks passed, and both panels completed all 4,500 oracle evaluations.

Strict best-parent beats increased from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 600/4,350 (13.79%), and mean child-minus-best-parent score improved from -0.100493 to -0.093989. Incumbent improvements were nearly unchanged, at 216 versus 218. Mean final-best score across tasks and seeds fell from 0.544374 to 0.524118, a paired change of -0.020256. Seed changes were -0.052822, -0.023812 and +0.015865; all five task means declined. Thus the intended allocation mechanism is confirmed, while the intended score increase was not observed.

finding_summary.headline: Core-balanced breeding broadened core use and raised parent-beating yield, but lowered final scores.
finding_summary.insights:
Equalizing core probability can reduce repeated use of abundant families without improving the best molecules found. The clearest coverage expansions were in decoration hopping and DRD2, yet their parent-beating counts and final-score means fell. Zaleplon breeding became more concentrated despite correct balancing within each selected band, showing that changing the conditional draw does not guarantee broader realized coverage once the evolving survivor population is considered.

The modest parent-beating gain also uses a weaker reference: mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.419645 to 0.395720, while mean evaluated-offspring score fell from 0.319152 to 0.301731. This relative yield gain therefore does not establish stronger offspring production. The number of admitted offspring later reused for breeding stayed almost unchanged, at 2,163 versus 2,167, and incumbent gains did not increase. The evidence narrows the problem to allocating toward productive surviving families rather than simply reducing their multiplicity imbalance; discarded or ineligible cores still receive no opportunity. The molecular assessment also shows that broader structural coverage continues to include repeated heterocycle growth, tiny fragments, reactive nitrogen-halogen/peroxide groups and strained fused rings. Murcko-core coverage alone does not resolve those quality limitations. Passive comparisons supply probabilities and parent identities, with no scores for alternate offspring or an alternate search trajectory.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation change executed correctly in all three replicas. Of 111,246 parent draws, 86,634 had unequal core multiplicities; every logged probability vector and inverse-CDF choice matched the intended rule. On the same eligible states and logged uniform variates, 36,398 selected parent ranks and 29,554 selected cores differed from the passive uniform comparator. Mean represented cores used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 14.60, and mean concentration of breeding uses fell from 0.299 to 0.189, measured as the sum of squared core-use shares. Coverage rose in 10 of 15 task/seed sessions; the effect was not universal. All accepted-state, survivor and pending-provenance checks passed, and both panels completed all 4,500 oracle evaluations.

Strict best-parent beats increased from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 600/4,350 (13.79%), and mean child-minus-best-parent score improved from -0.100493 to -0.093989. Incumbent improvements were nearly unchanged, at 216 versus 218. Mean final-best score across tasks and seeds fell from 0.544374 to 0.524118, a paired change of -0.020256. Seed changes were -0.052822, -0.023812 and +0.015865; all five task means declined. Thus the intended allocation mechanism is confirmed, while the intended score increase was not observed.

molecular_assessment.headline: Repeated heterocycle growth and tiny fragments coexist with reactive, highly fused leading molecules
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The current panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete three-seed Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9425 to 0.9931 and ring-closure presence from 0.977 to 0.9931; charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These are string-presence measurements, not aromatic atom fractions, ionization measurements or evidence of feasible stereochemistry. The output is ring-rich and often extensively aromatic: fused nitrogen carbonyl systems, aromatic amine/aminal frameworks and halogenated unsaturated heterocycles dominate the leaders. Chemical scale varies from tiny fragments to large assemblies of repeated heterocycles. This is particularly pronounced in deco_hop, whose mean SMILES length is 115.4 and maximum is 235; its seed-2 final molecules visibly repeat nitrogen-dione units. The Parent also produced reactive and extensively connected structures. Current leaders retain N-halogen bonds, peroxide or hypohalite motifs, tight ring fusion and unspecified configurations. Overall synthetic plausibility is questionable, with strongly implausible individual small-ring or growth outliers, and drug-like quality remains weak. Across-seed diversity is moderate; many late streams mainly elaborate a common core.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecules are moderately sized fused unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles bearing fluoroaryl carboxamides, alkyl/alkoxy substituents and hydroxymethyl or aminomethyl groups. Amide N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and fused-ring N-F are frequent in the leaders. Seed 0 reaches pyrazole thioamides with phenolic, cyclopentadienyl and cyclobutenyl groups; seed 1 reaches an aryl ketone with N-O/N-N functionality. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9782 and halogen presence is 0.7149. Relative to the Parent aromatic ketone, amide and thioheterocyclic families, the compact aromatic/carbonyl theme persists, with reactive nitrogen substitution and unusual ring geometry.
liabilities: N-Br, N-Cl and N-F bonds add reactivity to amide and ring nitrogens; N-O/N-N variants add compatibility concerns.
Unusual unsaturated small rings, scaffold doubling and very small fragment products reduce the chemical coherence of the output.
missing_features: Stable nonhalogenated nitrogen alternatives preserving the successful aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are poorly represented among the leading amide series.

Accessible fused-ring alternatives and explicit configurations or alkene geometry are absent for many unusual partially saturated and bridged products; a unique target pharmacophore cannot be inferred.

applicability_conditions: This is a feedback_memory parent-allocation experiment. The supplied blueprint permits changing parent allocation while accepted-memory interfaces, graph production, posterior inference and within-pool selection remain fixed.

The opportunity requires multiple accepted eligible core families with unequal survivor multiplicities inside the same inherited score band. This condition is directly present in the Parent's recorded three-replica states; no benefit is assumed for other tasks or initial populations.

Murcko grouping keeps scaffold atom and bond types but ignores stereochemical annotations and many peripheral substitutions. Equal scaffold mass is an allocation hypothesis, not a claim of equal pharmacology, synthetic accessibility, stability or medicinal relevance.

Acyclic molecules and explicit extraction failures remain full-identity groups. The mechanism consequently does not aggregate chemically related acyclic families and does not claim universal scaffold extraction on all generated chemistry.

Greedy survivor retention and the top-half breeding support are unchanged. The rule cannot revive discarded cores or assign probability to a core that has no eligible surviving member; equal mass within a band also does not imply equal mass across bands.

More represented cores may dilute repeated exploitation of a productive family. Final score and descendant efficiency require the protocol's paired evidence; passive same-state probability comparisons provide no missing oracle labels or full alternate search trajectory.

The recorded sibling stack and all supplied stable cluster definitions contain no core-multiplicity parent-allocation attempt. The posterior-selection cluster remains an inherited mechanism, not a revisited or removed selector. No active Round Injection or human research brief is supplied.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a population of at most sixty-four accepted molecules, kept in descending score order. It chooses a high-ranking score band and then a molecule uniformly within that band, produces a fresh surplus of crossover and mutation offspring, and uses correlated draws from a fingerprint Gaussian process to choose which offspring to evaluate. Every accepted score trains the posterior, even if its molecule leaves the breeding population. This loop reliably learns and selects, but most evaluated offspring do not improve on their generating parents, and successful molecular cores accumulate many close relatives.
approach.novelty: Give each represented molecular core equal breeding probability within the already selected score band. A core with many surviving analogues will share its probability among those analogues, while a less represented accepted core gains an opportunity to breed. The existing preference for high-scoring bands remains intact. The lineage's earlier child changed how generated offspring are selected for evaluation; this child changes only which accepted parents produce those offspring. Neither recorded sibling nor a supplied mechanism cluster has tested this conditional correction for core multiplicity.

research_intent.falsifier: The allocation mechanism is refuted if accepted-state provenance is violated, a selected parent is outside the unchanged eligible score band or excluded-partner rule, informative draws fail to assign equal total conditional mass to each represented core, actual choices fail their recorded inverse-CDF rule, or complete nondegenerate evidence shows no probability displacement and no realized change from the passive uniform law despite unequal eligible core multiplicities. If every eligible group has only one core or equal multiplicities, the opportunity is absent and the mechanism is inconclusive rather than demonstrated. Missing state/core/draw diagnostics also make activation inconclusive. A lower parent-beating fraction, narrower realized coverage under finite sampling, or worse final scores despite verified changed allocation is negative transfer evidence, not retrospective nonexecution. The component claim also fails if survivor admission, graph production, posterior inference or within-pool acquisition is changed beyond this declared parent-allocation mechanism.

research_intent.mechanism: Within each inherited score quantile, sample accepted breeding parents with probability inversely proportional to the number of eligible survivors sharing their Murcko core, so every represented core has equal conditional mass.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-fc2c108a5253 has complete accepted-feedback posterior selection on three replicas, with macro mean 0.5443738005952443 and population SD 0.013310111166991866, yet only 565 of 4350 selected offspring strictly beat their actual best generating parent.
